description: FUNCTION NUMVAL-C REJECTING a non-conforming argument, and what the program then does with the zero it yields. SDTMMI arrives as 'ab'; the store at :305-307 leaves WS-NUM-99 at zero and :307 writes '00' back into SDTMMI. '00' is numeric and is not greater than '12', so the month edit at :329-330 PASSES - the operator is not told the month is invalid. The composed start date is therefore '2026-00-15', and it is CALL 'CSUTLDTC' at :392 that rejects it: severity is not '0000' and the message number is 2517 (FC-INVALID-MONTH), which is not the tolerated '2513', so :400 reports 'Start Date - Not a valid date...' with the cursor on SDTMML. The normalised '00' is visible on the send, which is how the rejection is traceable to the store rather than to the edit. Expected values are STATICALLY DERIVED by reading app/cbl/CORPT00C.cbl, its copybooks, app/bms/CORPT00.bms and app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD - never captured from a COBOL run, which is impossible in this environment (risk R-A). Java has no transient data queue, so EXEC CICS WRITEQ TD QUEUE('JOBS') at :517 is reproduced through an explicit job-submission port; the eighty-byte content is identical and the dataset key JOBS names the TDQUEUE(JOBS) that app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD:499-505 defines as RECORDSIZE(80) RECORDFORMAT(FIXED) BLOCKFORMAT(UNBLOCKED) DISPOSITION(MOD).
